title: Stalemate

D0.outcome: Says that stalemate is a draw: the side to move is not in check but has no legal move.

D1.outcome: Tells checkmate from stalemate when told it is one of the two.

D2.outcome: In mixed positions names check, checkmate, stalemate or ongoing, and notices before moving when its own move would stalemate the enemy.

D3.outcome: In a won ending chooses the move that wins instead of stalemating, and knows that stalemate can save a lost game.

misconceptions: Stalemate is a win for the side that moved last.
Stalemate is the same as checkmate.
Having a big material lead means stalemate cannot happen.
conditions: Stalemate: the side to move is not in check and has no legal move; the game is drawn.
Before a move that boxes the king in, count the legal moves it has left.
contrasts: Same material, one move different: the king is attacked (mate, a win) or not attacked (stalemate, a draw).
How much extra material the stronger side has does not prevent stalemate.
